rounds.text: Nihar Info Global Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount to its sector, with a P/E ratio of 9.94x compared to the industry benchmark of 22.05x [E6]. This valuation gap is further underscored by a price-to-book ratio of 1.01x, which is less than half of the sector benchmark of 2.08x [E7]. The company has demonstrated a notable operational turnaround, evidenced by a massive 150 percentage point improvement in quarterly operating margins compared to the year-ago quarter [E31]. Furthermore, the company is currently generating an ROE of 10.22%, which successfully outperforms the sector benchmark of 9.89% [E9]. Conceded: the company has a history of poor long-term returns, including a median 3-year ROE of -27% and a 10-year median ROE of -6% [E26, E28]. Despite these historical challenges, the current valuation at 0.96x book value suggests the market has yet to price in the recent return to profitability [E2, E29].

The valuation of Nihar Info Global Ltd is undermined by a long-term track record of value destruction, as evidenced by a median return on equity of -6% over the last decade [E26]. This trend of poor performance has intensified in recent years, with the median return on equity plummeting to -13% over five years and -27% over three years [E27, E28]. The company’s inability to generate consistent returns is further highlighted by a low ROCE of 8.7% and an ROE of 8.7% [E12, E13]. Furthermore, the business is failing to improve its core profitability, as the operating margin has contracted from 6% to 5% over the last three years [E30]. Investors are also denied any immediate cash compensation for these risks, as the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: [E1, E2, E6, E7, E8, E9, E31].

The bear’s reliance on historical multi-year median ROE figures ignores the decisive operational turnaround currently underway, demonstrated by a remarkable quarterly operating margin surge of +150 percentage points to reach 3% in March 2026 compared to -147% in the year-ago quarter [E31]. Conceded: [E26, E27, E28, E30, E62]. While historical averages dragged down by past periods look weak, the company currently generates a positive ROE of 10.22% according to key-ratios data and 8.7% in filed statements, which actually outpaces the sector benchmark ROE of 9.89% [E9, E13]. Furthermore, claiming the valuation is undermined ignores the fact that the stock trades at an attractive P/E of just 9.94x against a sector benchmark of 22.05x, alongside a conservative P/B of 1.01x versus the sector's 2.08x [E6, E7]. The current price of ₹ 5.99 sits at a minor discount to its book value of ₹ 6.21 [E2], placing the market capitalisation at a modest ₹ 6.23 Cr [E3] while resting comfortably below the upper bound of its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: [E4, E12].

The bull points to a quarterly operating margin jump of +150 percentage points to 3% in March 2026 [E31], but this comes on the heels of a catastrophic -147% in the year-ago quarter [E31], and longer-term operating margins have actually compressed by 1 percentage point over three years [E30]. Conceded: [E31]. While the bull highlights current ROE figures of 10.22% and 8.7% [E9, E13], these single-period readings flatly contradict a devastating multi-year track record that includes a 3-year median ROE of -27% [E28], a 5-year median of -13% [E27], and a 10-year median of -6% [E26], earning the company an official negative flag for low ROE [E62]. The low valuation multiples and price-to-book ratio near parity [E2, E6, E7] are entirely justified by this chronic destruction of equity value rather than representing a hidden bargain. Furthermore, the bull admits the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], meaning shareholders receive zero cash return while enduring weak profitability metrics like an 8.7% ROCE [E12]. Finally, the micro-cap market capitalization of just ₹ 6.23 Cr [E3] combined with a stock sitting near the lower half of its 52-week range at 40% [E5] reflects persistent market skepticism toward these fleeting operational improvements.
